questions.stem: An inverter circuit is used to invert the input signal. If the input is a high voltage (1), what will be the output?
questions.solution: An inverter circuit takes a high input and produces a low output, or vice versa. So if the input is 1 (high), the output will be 0 (low).
questions.explanation: Inverters are basic logic gates that reverse the state of their input.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B (1) as the output, which would mean no inversion occurred. Remember, inverters change the signal's state.

questions.stem: An AND gate produces a high output only when both inputs are high. If Input A is 0 and Input B is 1, what will be the output?
questions.solution: An AND gate requires both inputs to be high for a high output. Since Input A is 0 and Input B is 1, the output will be 0.
questions.explanation: AND gates produce a high output only when all input signals are high.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B (1) as the output, which would occur if either or both inputs were high. Remember, both inputs must be high for an AND gate to output high.

questions.stem: An OR gate produces a high output when at least one input is high. If Input A is 1 and Input B is 0, what will be the output?
questions.solution: An OR gate produces a high output when at least one input is high. Since Input A is 1, the output will be 1, regardless of Input B being 0.
questions.explanation: OR gates produce a high output if any or all input signals are high.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A (0) as the output, which would occur if both inputs were low. Remember, at least one input must be high for an OR gate to output high.

questions.stem: A NOT gate can be implemented using a NAND gate by connecting its output back to its input. If the input is 0, what will be the output?
questions.solution: A NOT gate inverts its input. When implemented using a NAND gate, if the input is 0, the output of the NAND will be 1 (since both inputs are not high). This output is fed back to the input, effectively inverting it again and producing a high output.
questions.explanation: NOT gates can be constructed using other logic gates like NAND or NOR.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A (0) as the output, which would mean no inversion occurred. Remember, NOT gates invert their input.

questions.stem: A NOR gate produces a low output when both inputs are high. If both Input A and Input B are 1, what will be the output?
questions.solution: A NOR gate produces a low output when both inputs are high. Since both Input A and Input B are 1, the output will be 0.
questions.explanation: NOR gates produce a low output only when all input signals are high.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B (1) as the output, which would occur if either or both inputs were low. Remember, both inputs must be high for a NOR gate to output low.

questions.stem: A half-adder circuit has two inputs (A and B) and produces two outputs: Sum (S) and Carry (C). If Input A is 0 and Input B is 1, what will be the Sum output?
questions.solution: A half-adder calculates the sum of its two inputs using exclusive OR (XOR) and AND gates. When Input A is 0 and Input B is 1, the Sum output will be 1 (since 0 XOR 1 = 1).
questions.explanation: Half-adders are basic combinational circuits that add two bits.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A (0) as the sum, which would occur if both inputs were the same. Remember, a change in input bits results in a 1 in the Sum output for a half-adder.
